newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cera, Kredietbank merger talks progress.
newsitem.headline: Cera, Kredietbank merger talks progress.

text.p: Talks between Belgium's Cera Bank and Kredietbank about a merger, as precursor to a cooperation deal with Dutch Rabobank, are progressing, Belgian papers said on Wednesday.
Belgian financial daily L'Echo quoted the chairman of Belgian holding company Almanij, Jan Huyghebaert, as saying there was a certain logic to an alliance.
But he also said, "As long as there is no agreement about everything, there is no deal."

Belgian paper De Morgen said on Tuesday that there were no legal hurdles for an alliance of Cera and bourse-listed Kredietbank. The Kredietbank board concluded the cooperative structure of CERA was no barrier to a deal.
De Morgen said on Wednesday the economic feasibility of the merger was now being studied. The merger would create what it called a Belgian component equalling Rabobank in size.

A cooperation deal between the three would involve Kredietbank and Cera handling Belgian activities, Rabobank the Dutch side of the business, while international operations would be brought into a joint structure.
L'Echo quoted Huyghebaert as saying there would be no important announcements before September-October.
A Cera Bank spokesman had no comment on the reports.
"It is clear that we have thought of Cera, but there is no news to report, or no news that is ripe enough to be news," a Kredietbank spokesman was quoted as saying.
Through Almanij Cera and Kredietbank are linked already. Cera controls agricultural insurance ABB which is a major Almanij shareholder.
Both Kredietbank and Cera are focused on Flanders, Belgium Dutch-speaking northern half.

Accordingly, the papers said, a merger between the two was a natural alliance, which also made sense in the context of banks' stepped-up drive to achieve economies of scale and cut costs ahead of the introduction of Europe's single currency in 1999.
The launch of the euro is expected to boost competition among banks seeking to recoup margins lost as a result of the loss of forex trading volmues.
Rabobank, itself a cooperative bank, has spoken of exploratory talks with Cera and Kredietbank. But it has ruled out a full merger between the three.

There have also been reports that Kredietbank would link up with CCF of France, acting as a white knight to thwart a possible takeover of CCF by Germany's Deutsche Bank, which says it is considering acquiring a French partner.
